title: Finite flat descent of regular divisor purity in invertible degree
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite locally free morphism of constant positive rank $d$ with $\ell\nmid d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] between regular Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular effective Cartier divisor and suppose the reduced inverse image $D'=(Y\times_XD)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is also a regular effective Cartier divisor, with inclusion $i'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Effective Cartier means locally cut out by one nonzerodivisor. If
$$A_{D'}\to i'^!A_Y(1)[2]$$
is an isomorphism, then so is
$$A_D\to i^!A_X(1)[2].$$
No assumption that $f$ is generically etale is made.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.3, printed p.246 (the divisor descent assertion itself).

proof.text: We compute at arbitrary geometric points of the two given regular pairs $(X,D)$ and $(Y,D')$. Write either pair as $(W,Z)$, choose $\bar w\to Z$, and put $S=W_{(\bar w)}=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $E=Z\times_WS$, $U=S\setminus E$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], $R$ is the algebraic strict henselization of $\mathcal O_{W,w}$. Thus it is strictly henselian, Noetherian and regular by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian, lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]. Choose a divisor equation $f$ on an affine chart containing $w$, and let $t\in R$ be its image. The structural map is flat by [lem-sbc-affine-strict-henselization-structural-flat]. Applying the injective-tensor definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] to multiplication by the nonzerodivisor $f$ shows that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective. The tensor identifications are $R\otimes_BB=R$ on this chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$. The closed-localization comparison [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] identifies $R/(t)$ with the strict-local ring of $Z$; the same affine comparison and regularity lemmas, applied to $\mathcal O_{Z,w}$, make this quotient regular. We have $t\in\mathfrak m_R$, $\ell\in R^\times$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/t]$.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.3, strict localization; Stacks 06LN and 05WS. The nonzerodivisor argument applies the injective-tensor definition, not the excluded lci calculus.

proof.text: Both $R$ and $R/(t)$ are domains by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]; hence $(t)$ is a proper prime ideal and $t\ne0$. Put $B=R[1/t]$. The fraction description [def-weil-ring-localization-away] makes $R\to B$ injective and $B$ a nonzero domain. Its zero prime belongs to every nonempty basic open, so $U$ is connected and nonempty. For $v=x/t^a\in B^\times$ write $v^{-1}=y/t^b$; then $xy=t^{a+b}$. Induction on $N$ proves that $xy=t^N$ implies $x=ut^c$ for a unit $u$ and $0\le c\le N$: for $N=0$, $xy=1$; for $N>0$, primality of $(t)$ puts $t$ in one factor, cancel it and apply induction. Thus $v=ut^m$, $m=c-a\in\mathbf Z$. If $ut^m=u't^{m'}$ with $m>m'$, then $u'=ut^{m-m'}\in(t)$, a contradiction; exchanging the roles treats $m<m'$. Equality of exponents gives $u=u'$. Therefore $B^\times=R^\times\times t^{\mathbf Z}$ as a group, and multiplication adds the displayed exponents.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, low-degree algebra; Stacks 00NP (algebra-lemma-regular-domain). The unit calculation is a direct induction using primality.

proof.text: The group $R^\times$ is $\ell$-divisible. For $u\in R^\times$, $X^\ell-u$ reduces to a separable polynomial over the separably closed residue field: its derivative is nonzero at every root because $u$ and $\ell$ are units. It has a simple nonzero residue root; [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] lifts it to $a\in R$ with $a^\ell=u$. The lift is a unit with inverse $a^{\ell-1}u^{-1}$. Also [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity] supplies a generator $\zeta\in\mu_\ell(R)$, whose distinct powers have unit differences. Successively dividing by monic factors and cancelling these unit differences proves $X^\ell-1=\prod_{a=0}^{\ell-1}(X-\zeta^a)$. On any etale test scheme $T\to S$, a root $y$ equals exactly one $\zeta^a$ locally: the opens where every $y-\zeta^b$, $b\ne a$, is a unit cover $T$, are disjoint, and the product identity forces $y=\zeta^a$ there. Conversely such locally constant choices glue. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ identifies $A_S$ with $\mu_{\ell,S}$, and likewise on $U$ and every further pullback. Since $U$ is connected, its locally constant $A$-valued maps are constant. Thus $H^0(U,A)=A$ and the restriction $\mu_\ell(R)\to H^0(U,\mu_\ell)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, degree zero and roots-of-unity trivialization; Stacks 04GF/04GG, 03P5 and section-kummer.

proof.text: Every line bundle $L$ on $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is trivial. It is quasi-coherent and Zariski locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. Put $P=\Gamma(U,L)$; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] gives $\widetilde P\simeq L$. Refine local trivializations to basic opens $D(b_i)$. Affine quasi-compactness [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] gives a finite subcover; the $b_i$ generate the unit ideal, since a maximal ideal containing them all would be an uncovered point. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], $P_{b_i}\simeq B_{b_i}$. The finite basic-open criterion [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-projective] makes $P$ finite projective. At each prime one $b_i$ is invertible, so $P$ has local rank one everywhere. The algebraic result [lem-trf-regular-local-pic-zero], applied to the regular local ring $R$ and element $t$, now gives $P\simeq B$. Applying tilde and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] in rank one gives $L\simeq\mathcal O_U$. Thus $\operatorname{Pic}(U)=0$, without assuming $B$ is local.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, degree-one input reconstructed from Stacks 0AFZ (more-algebra-lemma-regular-local-Pic-zero), 01HV/01IA and 00NX.

proof.text:
Hilbert 90 on arbitrary schemes [thm-sc-hilbert-90] identifies $H^1(U,\mathbf G_m)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(U)$, hence it is zero. Use the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] on $U$ (where $\ell$ is a unit). Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder], specialized to $\mathrm{id}_U$, gives the exact segment
$$B^\times\xrightarrow{(-)^\ell}B^\times\xrightarrow\delta H^1(U,\mu_\ell)\to0.$$
By Steps 2 and 3, its cokernel is $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$, with the exponent of $t$ modulo $\ell$ as coordinate: the $R^\times$ factor has zero cokernel. Thus $\kappa(t)=\delta(t)$ freely generates the $A$-module $H^1(U,A(1))$. Explicitly $ut^m$ maps to $m\kappa(t)$, because $u$ is an $\ell$-th power. Together with Step 3 this supplies both low degrees, with the actual Kummer generator.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, low-degree computation; Stacks 03P8 (theorem-hilbert-90) and 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence).

proof.text:
Return to the original pair $(W,Z)$ and let $j:W-Z\hookrightarrow W$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$. Apply [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] to $A_W(1)$, then the cohomology exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and exact geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. The closed stalk of the first term is the stalk on $Z$ by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar]. The immersion $j$ is qcqs: on each affine divisor chart its inverse image is the affine principal open $D(f)$; these charts give the local quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness conditions. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] identifies the third term in degree $q$ with $H^q(U,A(1))$, for the $U$ of Step 1. The middle term has only degree zero, $\mu_\ell(R)$, and restriction to $H^0(U,A(1))$ is the isomorphism of Step 3. The exact sequence gives
$$\mathcal H^m(i^!A_W(1))_{\bar w}=0\ (m\le1),\qquad \mathcal H^m(i^!A_W(1))_{\bar w}\simeq H^{m-1}(U,A(1))\ (m\ge2).$$
These latter identifications are the localization connecting maps. In particular the twist-shifted target has no negative stalk cohomology, degree zero $A\kappa(t)$, and degree $r>0$ equal to $H^{r+1}(U,A(1))$. No exchange theorem for $i^!$ under strict localization is assumed.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, reconstruct the strict-local test using Stacks 0A45 and 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images).

proof.text: We check the actual map's degree-zero generator, rather than just the rank of its target. By the $c=1$ clause of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] (with $n=1$, $\Lambda_1=A$) the divisor map of the statement is the $Ri_*\dashv i^!$ transpose of the map $c_{Z,A}$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], i.e. of the supported Kummer class of $\mathcal O_W(Z)$ with its canonical off-divisor frame; its defining relative extension and coefficient splice are [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. On a principal chart its global frame is $e=f^{-1}$, while its canonical off-divisor section is $s=1=f e$. Thus in the frame torsor $s=f\cdot e$. Apply [lem-pur-principal-torsor-yoneda-sign] with $G=\mathbf G_m$, $g=f$ and the Kummer coefficient sequence. It identifies this very relative extension's splice with $-\partial\delta(f)$ under the supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]. The sign depends only on the fixed extension convention and is a unit. The formula first restricts to etale divisor charts by that node's naturality. Under the canonical strict-local restriction of Step 6, clause 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] sends $\delta(f)$ to $\delta(t)=\kappa(t)$; the localization connecting map is precisely the map used in Step 6. Thus the original class sends $1$ to $-\kappa(t)$ under that identification. Exact forgetting and the scalar-root map in the boundary definition leave this generator unchanged for $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Hence the degree-zero stalk map is an isomorphism, including $\ell=2$. This uses the permitted principal-torsor formula, with no appeal to the excluded supported-Yoneda node.

source.place: XVI section 2.1 and Proposition 3.4.2; Stacks 03PL, sites-cohomology 03AJ, derived 06XU, and the existing generic principal-frame signed formula.

proof.text: For both given pairs and every geometric point of their divisors, Steps 1–7 now compute the cohomology of the actual class map. The source has only degree zero; the map in degree zero is an isomorphism; its target has no negative degrees. It is an isomorphism on all stalk cohomology precisely when $H^q(U,A(1))=0$ for all $q\ge2$. The root-of-unity trivialization of Step 3 identifies this with $H^q(U,A)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] to these bounded-below class maps on $Z$. Therefore the assumed isomorphism for $(Y,D')$ implies vanishing on every one of its strict-local complements. Conversely, to prove the desired isomorphism for $(X,D)$ it suffices to show vanishing on all its strict-local complements. This implication has been proved from the localization sequence and the low-degree calculation in the preceding steps; it cites no excluded criterion.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, conclude the explicit stalk calculation by conservativity.

proof.text:
Fix now $\bar x\to D$ and the corresponding $S,U$ from Step 1 for $(X,D)$. By [lem-trf-finite-base-strict-localization],
$$Y\times_XS\simeq\coprod_a Y_{(\bar y_a)},$$
where the index set is the finite set of geometric points of $Y_{\bar x}$. Every $\bar y_a$ is in the underlying set of $D'$ because that set is the inverse image of $D$. By [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian], $D'\times_YY_{(\bar y_a)}=D'_{(\bar y_a)}$ as closed schemes. Their underlying sets are also the inverse images of $D$; hence
$$V:=Y\times_XU\simeq\coprod_a\bigl(Y_{(\bar y_a)}-D'_{(\bar y_a)}\bigr).$$
Step 8 applied to the assumed pure pair $(Y,D')$ makes each summand's $H^q(-,A)$ zero for $q\ge2$. A sheaf on a finite disjoint union is a tuple of sheaves; monomorphisms and their lifts into injectives are componentwise. Thus a tuple of injective resolutions is an injective resolution on the union. Its section complex is their finite product, whose kernels and images are componentwise. The definition [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] then gives $H^q(V,A)=0$ for $q\ge2$.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.3, finite strict-local decomposition; Stacks 05WR, 0GIP and 03QP.

proof.text: Write $g:V\to U$. It is finite locally free of rank $d$. Indeed, [lem-pc-flf-properties] gives finite free charts of rank $d$ for $f_*\mathcal O_Y$, and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] describes every affine base change by tensor product; tensoring the chart basis gives a basis of the same rank. These chart algebras are flat and finitely presented (their multiplication table on a finite basis gives finitely many algebra generators and relations), so satisfy [def-pc-finite-locally-free] also after any etale base change $W_0\to U$. Use [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts] on $g_{W_0}$ to define the norm $N_{W_0}(b)$ of a section $b$ of its structure sheaf. Norms commute with maps of etale test schemes: on a finite free affine chart the multiplication matrix becomes its coefficientwise image after scalar extension, and its determinant polynomial does likewise. The uniqueness and scalar-extension characterization in [lem-a1-principal-free-algebra-determinant-norm] make these equalities independent of bases and charts; sheaf equality glues them. Thus these norms have the restriction compatibility needed for a map on small-etale sheaves.

source.place: XVI Lemma 3.4.4, reconstruct the splitting by the determinant norm of Stacks 0BD2 (divisors-lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm).

proof.text: On every rank-$d$ chart, multiplication matrices satisfy $M_{bc}=M_bM_c$ and $M_1=I_d$. By [lem-sfb-matrix-cramer-determinant-identities], norms satisfy $N(bc)=N(b)N(c)$ and $N(1)=1$. Units therefore have unit norms. If $b^\ell=1$, then $N(b)^\ell=N(b^\ell)=1$, so we get a sheaf homomorphism $N:g_*\mu_{\ell,V}\to\mu_{\ell,U}$. For a section $a\in\mu_\ell(W_0)$ the multiplication matrix of its pullback is $aI_d$, with determinant $a^d$. Hence the composite of pullback and norm is the $d$-th power map. Transport using $1\mapsto\zeta$ from Step 3 to obtain an additive map $\tau:g_*A_V\to A_U$ with $\tau\eta=d\,\mathrm{id}$, where $\eta:A_U\to g_*A_V$ is the pullback unit. Any additive map between groups killed by the prime $\ell$ commutes with multiplication by integers modulo $\ell$, so this map is $A$-linear. Since $\ell\nmid d$, $d^{-1}\tau$ is a retraction of $\eta$. This uses the original finite-free rank, not a degree of the reduced inverse image.

source.place: XVI Lemma 3.4.4, scalar composite; determinant norm and scalar-matrix computation in Stacks 0BD2.

proof.text: Finite direct image is exact [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], so $Rg_*A_V=g_*A_V$. Under the canonical Leray isomorphism $R\Gamma(U,Rg_*A_V)\simeq R\Gamma(V,A_V)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-leray-composition], pullback is $H^q(R\Gamma(U,\eta))$. Applying $R\Gamma(U,-)$ and then $H^q$ to $(d^{-1}\tau)\eta=\mathrm{id}$ supplies a left inverse. Thus $H^q(U,A)\to H^q(V,A)$ is injective for every $q\ge0$. Step 9 makes the target zero for $q\ge2$, so the source vanishes in those degrees. Since $\bar x$ was arbitrary, Step 8 proves the desired isomorphism of the Kummer class map on $D$. If $D$ is empty, its derived category is zero and the conclusion holds immediately. The norm calculation applies to ramified and inseparable finite locally free maps, so no generic-etaleness hypothesis has been introduced.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.3, final injectivity and descent; Stacks 03QP and the Leray comparison.
